decisions.decision: Adopt the full feature set and priority order exactly as given: interruption correctness > backlink graph integrity > honest permission degradation, complete-over-broad, offline-first absolute for all core features.
decisions.rationale: Preserves user intent and prevents scope creep from silently reordering priorities.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all 11 features as equally weighted
constraints: No later phase may reprioritize without flagging it as an explicit deviation

decisions.decision: Interruption-handling claims must name the specific scenario and test method used; phone-call and Bluetooth-route-change scenarios require a real device, background/memory-pressure can only be approximated in Simulator.
decisions.rationale: Simulator cannot produce real phone calls or Bluetooth route changes, so unqualified 'interruption handled' claims would be unverifiable.
rejected_alternatives: Accepting a blanket 'interruptions handled' claim without scenario detail
constraints: Build/verify phases must list which scenarios were tested and how

decisions.decision: Widget, Live Activity, Share Extension, and App Intents must read/write the same local store as the main app via an App Group + shared SwiftData model container.
decisions.rationale: Without a shared store these surfaces would have to fake data or show nothing, violating the no-placeholder-data rule even though the user didn't name App Groups explicitly.
rejected_alternatives: Letting each extension keep its own isolated store
constraints: Treat App Group setup as a hard requirement, not optional plumbing

decisions.decision: 'No orphaned Live Activity on kill' is implemented as staleDate-at-request-time plus reconciliation-on-next-launch that ends any stale activity found.
decisions.rationale: iOS has no guaranteed clean-shutdown hook on force-kill, so this is the only mechanism that can actually deliver on the promise.
rejected_alternatives: Promising real-time cleanup at the moment of force-kill
constraints: Verification of this requirement must reference staleDate + relaunch reconciliation, not a live kill-detection claim

decisions.decision: When on-device Speech recognition is unavailable for the current locale, recording stays enabled and the entry shows an explicit 'transcription unavailable on-device for this language' state; the app never falls back to server recognition and never silently produces an empty transcript.
decisions.rationale: The user's word 'flag' is not itself a UI behavior; this makes it concrete and testable.
rejected_alternatives: Disabling recording entirely when on-device Speech is unavailable
Silently transcribing with no visible indicator
constraints: Any locale/device where supportsOnDeviceRecognition is false must show this state, verifiable in-app

decisions.decision: HealthKit is documented as usable for on-device/local testing under a free personal developer team, with a separate caveat that TestFlight/App Store distribution requires a paid account — not treated as a single blanket Gap.
decisions.rationale: Conflating local testing capability with distribution capability would misstate what actually works in this environment.
rejected_alternatives: Marking HealthKit as fully blocked
Ignoring the distribution-tier distinction
constraints: Gap documentation for HealthKit must state both tiers explicitly

decisions.decision: Search relevance ranking must be a written, checkable formula with a concrete two-entry test case demonstrating expected ordering.
decisions.rationale: Prevents shipping weighted substring matching disguised as a 'relevance score.'
rejected_alternatives: Accepting any non-substring ordering as sufficient
constraints: The formula must be documented in a later phase and testable by hand against a known corpus

decisions.decision: Backlinks are never stored, only computed live by scanning existing entries for mentions of the target entry's ID; deleting an entry automatically removes it from all live backlink queries with no extra bookkeeping. A forward @-mention pointing at a since-deleted entry renders as a visually distinct 'broken link' indicator rather than silently becoming plain text.
decisions.rationale: Live computation structurally prevents dangling/duplicate reverse-backlinks, which is the integrity bar the user set; honestly surfacing a broken forward-mention respects the same 'never hide state' principle without reintroducing stored/desyncable backlink records.
rejected_alternatives: Storing backlinks as a separately maintained list
Silently converting a dead mention to plain text
constraints: No backlink data may be persisted as a separate maintained table/list; it must always be a live query result

decisions.decision: Demo entries are seeded and removed via one explicit Settings toggle, visually/data-model distinct from real entries at all times.
decisions.rationale: Prevents demo data from ever being mistaken for or mixed into real user data.
rejected_alternatives: Auto-seeding demo data on first launch without an explicit toggle
constraints: Toggle state must be reversible and never partially apply

decisions.decision: CarPlay scene code path is implemented in full but recorded as an explicit Gap because the CarPlay audio-app entitlement is unavailable on a free personal developer account.
decisions.rationale: Matches the user's own instruction for this exact case — build correctly, document rather than fake or omit.
rejected_alternatives: Omitting CarPlay entirely
Claiming CarPlay works without the entitlement
constraints: Gap entry must state what the entitlement is and what obtaining it would require

decisions.decision: Use TimeInterval/Double for all durations and Int for counts; no Decimal usage anywhere in this app.
decisions.rationale: User explicitly ruled out the money-precision pattern from prior apps since there is no currency here.
rejected_alternatives: Applying Decimal to durations or scores by default habit
constraints: Any numeric field must be justified as Int/Double/TimeInterval, not Decimal, unless a future phase introduces a genuinely decimal-precision need

decisions.decision: The 'no orphaned Live Activity' guarantee is stated with its honest residual window: no orphan once the app has a chance to reconcile (staleDate + relaunch reconciliation), backstopped by iOS's own staleness dimming — not a zero-window guarantee if the device sits untouched after a force-quit.
decisions.rationale: The mechanism (staleDate + reconciliation) is correct but stating it as fully solved without the residual window would be an overclaim a later phase could exploit to call the requirement done when a real gap remains.
rejected_alternatives: Stating the requirement as fully solved with no caveat
constraints: Any claim that this requirement is satisfied must include the residual-window caveat in its evidence

decisions.decision: HealthKit reads work normally in the iOS Simulator via manually-entered sample data in the Simulator's Health app; only App Store/TestFlight distribution is gated behind a paid developer account, not local or Simulator testing.
decisions.rationale: Factual correction — conflating HealthKit with CarPlay's true entitlement gate would cause the run guide to skip a test that is actually possible now, under-claiming a gap that doesn't exist.
rejected_alternatives: Treating HealthKit as device-only/untestable in this environment like CarPlay
constraints: The Simulator run guide must test HealthKit locally and only note the distribution-tier caveat, not a testing-tier caveat

decisions.decision: @-mentions and backlinks resolve via the target entry's persistent UUID, never by matching display-title text; renaming an entry must never break or misdirect any existing mention of it.
decisions.rationale: Title-based matching would silently break links on rename or, worse, misdirect a mention to a different entry that now shares the old title — a real-world bug a quick demo walkthrough wouldn't catch. Raised independently by both participants.
rejected_alternatives: Resolving mentions by matching current entry title text
constraints: Data model must store a stable identifier reference for every mention, not a string match

decisions.decision: Transcript sentence-to-audio-timestamp anchors are immutable once created; user text edits are represented as overlay deltas on top of the anchor set; audio seek always resolves via anchor ID, never a raw string/character index.
decisions.rationale: This is the concrete mechanism that makes tap-to-seek survive a transcript edit, closing the desync risk flagged in round 1 with an actual implementation rule rather than just a stated intention.
rejected_alternatives: Recomputing anchor positions by re-diffing edited text against original string offsets
constraints: Any transcript edit path must preserve anchor IDs; seek logic must never index by character/string position

decisions.decision: The interruption-correctness success metric requires at least one clean verified pass of each named scenario (real incoming call, Siri invocation, backgrounding, force-quit via app switcher during active recording, and low-storage condition if feasible), in addition to 20+ total manual runs.
decisions.rationale: An undifferentiated rep count can be satisfied by repeating the easiest scenario 20 times; naming the scenario mix prevents gaming the metric.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the metric as an unqualified '20+ manual runs'
constraints: Test evidence must show a pass/fail per named scenario, not just a total run count

decisions.decision: Entries without a transcript yet (on-device Speech unavailable, or transcription still running) remain findable via tags, mood, and sketch metadata in search; this is documented expected behavior, not a defect.
decisions.rationale: Without this documented, a build-verification pass could misdiagnose expected behavior as a search bug.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving untranscribed-entry search behavior undocumented and implicit
constraints: Search spec/documentation must state this explicitly

decisions.decision: Every later phase reports each numbered requirement's status as guaranteed / degrades / gapped with supporting evidence (a 'feature health card'), rather than a bare 'done' claim; a phase is not handoff-ready until every requirement has both status and evidence.
decisions.rationale: Prevents 'it compiles' from being mistaken for 'it works' across an app with this much lifecycle/permission complexity.
rejected_alternatives: Accepting a simple done/not-done checklist without evidence
constraints: Build and verification phases must produce this per-requirement status+evidence artifact before the phase is considered complete

decisions.decision: Frame the audience as a privacy-first solo journaler capturing voice notes during interrupted real-world moments, overlapping Day One/Daylio (mood journaling) and Obsidian/Roam (backlink graph) user bases.
decisions.rationale: Both participants independently converged on this reading of the feature list; it explains why voice+graph+mood in one app is the product's actual value rather than a random feature bundle.
rejected_alternatives: Treating this as a general-purpose notes/productivity app with no specific audience lens
constraints: This audience framing is an explicitly labeled ASSUMPTION (no external research fetched) and should be treated as inference, not fact, by later phases

decisions.decision: The product's real competitive differentiator is the combination of voice + timeline-anchored transcript + tags/mood + live backlinks + HealthKit context in one offline graph — not on-device transcription alone, since Apple's own Voice Memos already ships that.
decisions.rationale: Prevents the team from pitching or prioritizing on-device transcription as if it were novel; the actual gap is the cross-category combination.
rejected_alternatives: Treating on-device transcription as the primary differentiator
constraints: Later phases' feature framing/marketing copy should lead with the combination, not transcription alone

decisions.decision: The true shippable v1 is the core loop only (record, interruption-safe finalize/resume, on-device transcribe, tag/mood suggestions, live backlinks, documented-relevance search), built on top of the App Group + shared SwiftData container as foundational infrastructure; widget/Live Activity are next tier, Share Extension/App Intents are secondary, CarPlay is code-path-only with zero polish time.
decisions.rationale: Eleven features plus four extension surfaces is a portfolio of apps, not a first build; both participants independently proposed the same build-order fix, and it directly serves the prompt contract's existing priority order (interruption correctness > backlinks > honest degradation).
rejected_alternatives: Building all 11 features and all extension surfaces to equal depth in the first pass
constraints: Build phase must sequence work so the App Group/shared-store foundation is built once before widget/Live Activity/Share Extension/App Intents are attempted, not retrofitted after

decisions.decision: HealthKit's denied/not-connected state is designed as the default, primary visual state, not a fallback edge case.
decisions.rationale: Reviewers won't have real sleep/activity history matched to demo journal entries unless it's specifically hand-seeded into the Simulator's Health app, so the not-connected path is what most review passes will actually exercise.
rejected_alternatives: Designing the HealthKit-connected state as primary and treating denial as a secondary/edge path
constraints: Design phase must give the not-connected state full visual treatment, not a bare placeholder

decisions.decision: NaturalLanguage sentiment output must be presented in the UI as a rough polarity signal (small score/label), never implied to be a clinical or deep understanding of the user's emotional state.
decisions.rationale: Overclaiming emotional understanding in a journaling app specifically erodes trust fast; NaturalLanguage's sentiment API is coarse positive/negative/neutral polarity, not a mood-clinical measure.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting mood score with language implying deeper emotional analysis
constraints: Design/copy for mood UI must use modest, hedged language (e.g. 'rough signal') rather than authoritative framing

decisions.decision: The CarPlay entitlement gap note must be fact-checked in a later phase rather than asserting that a paid developer account alone unlocks it — it may also require a separate Apple approval/request step.
decisions.rationale: Both participants flagged this as currently an unverified assumption; if wrong, the gap documentation would overpromise what upgrading the account tier alone would fix.
rejected_alternatives: Asserting as fact that a paid account is sufficient to unlock CarPlay
constraints: The Gap entry for CarPlay must be verified/confirmed, not just repeated from this phase's assumption, before being stated as fact in build or verification phases

decisions.decision: Demo seed data must include at least one HealthKit-correlated day and one broken-link (mention pointing at a deleted entry) example specifically.
decisions.rationale: These are the two honest-degradation/edge states most likely to go completely unseen in a normal review pass otherwise.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving demo data generic without guaranteeing these two specific states are represented
constraints: Demo entries seed logic must guarantee these two scenarios exist, not leave them to chance

decisions.decision: Fieldnotes is built as a single cohesive app, not split into a portfolio of sibling projects.
decisions.rationale: The prompt names one product with one value proposition; the widget, Live Activity, Share Extension, App Intents, and CarPlay scene are all required surfaces of that same product that must share one local SwiftData store per the prompt contract's App Group requirement — splitting them into separate apps would break backlink integrity, audio resume/finalization invariants, and transcript anchor behavior, and would recreate exactly the 'fake cross-target sync' failure mode the contract forbids.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting widget/Live Activity/Share Extension/CarPlay into independent sibling apps
Wrapping this as a parent/child portfolio because it has multiple entry points/targets
constraints: No portfolio-json manifest is produced for this run
Later phases must treat this as one repo/project with multiple targets sharing one App Group + SwiftData model container, not separate projects

decisions.decision: Selected app record: slug 'fieldnotes', category journaling / personal-knowledge / wellness, build=true, promise = offline-first interrupt-safe voice capture + editable timeline-anchored transcript + mood/tag suggestions + live backlinks + documented search + local HealthKit context, target user = privacy-first solo journaler needing reliable capture through real-life interruptions.
decisions.rationale: Directly reflects the prompt and the already-converged product_research framing; gives later phases a single unambiguous app identity to build against.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the app identity implicit rather than recording it as a discrete selection record
constraints: Build phase must use this slug/category/promise/target-user as the canonical app record

decisions.decision: The single-app, core-loop-first framing is a build-order and attention-allocation decision, not a scope reduction — all 11 numbered features plus the 4 extension surfaces plus CarPlay remain in scope, each required to land as either fully working or an honestly named Gap.
decisions.rationale: Reaffirming 'narrow core first' strongly could otherwise be misread downstream as quietly cutting features 7-11; the contract's production-ready bar (DEC-prompt_contract-018 feature health cards) already requires every requirement to have a status, so this phase clarifies sequencing intent doesn't change that bar.
rejected_alternatives: Letting build-order emphasis stand without clarifying it isn't a scope cut, risking later phases dropping features silently
constraints: Build phase must still attempt every one of the 11 features and 4 extension surfaces plus CarPlay, sequenced core-first, and report each via the feature health card format

decisions.decision: Product promise: Fieldnotes is an offline-first iOS voice journal that reliably captures diary entries through real-world interruptions and makes them recallable via timeline-anchored editable transcripts, tags, mood signals, live backlinks, and local HealthKit context, with zero backend/account/network dependency and no faked feature state.
decisions.rationale: Both participants independently converged on 'trust under interruption' as the one-sentence core of the app rather than any single feature (transcription, tagging, etc.) being the headline.
rejected_alternatives: Framing the promise around on-device transcription or mood tracking as the headline feature
constraints: Later phases must treat interruption-safety and honest state as the product's core identity, not one feature among eleven

decisions.decision: Primary user is a privacy-first solo journaler capturing short (30s-3min) unplanned bursts during real-world interruption-prone moments; the defining scenario is recovery from a mid-recording interruption, not the happy path.
decisions.rationale: Directly restates and locks in product_research's audience framing as the design target for this phase.
rejected_alternatives: Designing primarily around the uninterrupted happy-path recording flow
constraints: UI/UX decisions must be judged against the interruption-recovery scenario first, happy path second

decisions.decision: Core loop is: record (with live waveform) -> stop or auto-finalize on interruption -> async non-blocking on-device transcription with a visible per-entry state (transcribing/unavailable/ready) -> editable anchor-based transcript with tap-to-seek -> dismissible/acceptable tag+mood suggestions -> optional UUID-based @-mention with live backlinks.
decisions.rationale: Synthesizes Codex's functional loop with Claude's requirement that transcription be async/queued so a second recording is never blocked, and that the entry list surface an honest per-entry readiness state.
rejected_alternatives: Blocking the UI or new recordings until the current entry finishes transcribing
constraints: Timeline list must show a per-entry transcribing/unavailable/ready indicator; recording a new entry must never be blocked by a prior entry's in-progress transcription

decisions.decision: Information architecture is three tabs (Timeline, Search, Settings) with Entry Detail as a pushed screen (pinned audio player + scrollable transcript + footer stack for tags/mood/sketch/backlinks); no separate graph-visualization screen — backlinks render inline only.
decisions.rationale: Search is a named, documented, relevance-ranked feature and deserves a real tab rather than being buried; a literal graph view was never requested and would be scope creep the build can't afford.
rejected_alternatives: Burying search as an icon within Timeline
Adding a fourth tab or screen for a node-graph visualization of backlinks
constraints: Build/design phases must implement exactly these three tabs plus pushed entry detail; no graph-visualization screen is in scope

decisions.decision: Hard scope boundaries: no cloud sync/accounts/server processing/analytics/telemetry/third-party SDKs/IAP ever; Share Extension is one-way import only (not outbound sharing to people); audio is append-only per entry (only transcript text is editable, no trim/splice); CarPlay gets zero visual polish time; widget and Live Activity each ship one fixed layout with no user configuration for v1.
decisions.rationale: Prevents scope creep into monetization, social/sharing features, or audio-editing complexity that was never requested and would dilute build time away from the interruption-safety and backlink-integrity priorities.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing raw audio trim/splice editing
Building configurable widget sizes/layouts for v1
Treating Share Extension as bidirectional sharing
constraints: Any future request for these excluded capabilities must be treated as new scope requiring explicit re-discussion, not silently added

decisions.decision: Measurable success criteria are stated as build-verification-checkable tests: 5 named interruption scenarios each with >=1 clean pass across 20+ total runs (per-scenario reporting); tap-to-seek accuracy <=300ms tolerance surviving transcript edits; zero dangling/duplicate backlinks after delete with visible broken-link state on stale forward mentions; documented relevance ordering verified against a fixed two-entry test case; every permission-gated feature verified by actually toggling the permission off, not by code inspection alone.
decisions.rationale: Vibe-checkable criteria ('interruptions handled', 'search works') would let a later phase claim success without real evidence; each criterion here is phrased so a verification phase can pass/fail it concretely.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving success criteria as qualitative/aggregate statements
constraints: Build verification phase must produce evidence against each of these five criteria specifically, not a general impression of quality

decisions.decision: Amend DEC-initial_discussion-005's 'no IAP/monetization ever' boundary narrowly to allow a Fieldnotes Pro subscription, with three hard constraints: it may never gate any of the 11 numbered core features, never gate a user's own recorded data, and never require network for anything the free tier already does offline.
decisions.rationale: This phase's playbook requires real, functional subscription value; the original prompt never banned monetization, only our own earlier phrasing did, so this is a narrow correction rather than overriding user intent.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'no monetization ever' standing and failing this phase's acceptance check
Allowing broad monetization without the data/feature-gating constraints
constraints: Free tier ships all 11 numbered features with zero caps forever
Subscription state must never block access to a user's own past entries, transcripts, tags, or base search

decisions.decision: Fieldnotes Pro consists of: on-device Insights (mood trend, tag frequency, recording cadence), advanced search (saved searches, compound tag+mood+date filters, search history), unlimited sketches per entry (free tier capped at one), and extra app icons/themes — all computed from data already in the local store with no new capture or permission.
decisions.rationale: Needed to be a concrete, checkable feature set (functional utility, not cosmetic) rather than an abstract 'premium tier' placeholder, satisfying the phase's acceptance check that subscription value be functional.
rejected_alternatives: Cosmetic-only paid tier (themes/icons alone)
Gating any of the numbered 1-11 features behind Pro
constraints: On subscription lapse, Insights/advanced search grey out with an explanation but core data and base search continue working unchanged

decisions.decision: Subscription purchase requires one StoreKit network round-trip at time of purchase only; all subsequent entitlement checks use Transaction.currentEntitlements locally, verified by a named manual test case: cold airplane-mode launch immediately after purchase must show Pro as active.
decisions.rationale: Prevents 'subscription works' from being a vibe-checked claim; makes the offline-after-purchase requirement concretely testable in build verification.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing periodic network re-validation of entitlement, which would violate the offline-first contract
constraints: This test case must be carried into the build-verification checklist explicitly

decisions.decision: Add one narrow carve-out to the no-multi-user/no-sharing-between-people boundary: a user-initiated 'share this entry as a card' export (mood + tags + short snippet only, never full transcript or audio) to the system share sheet, as the app's niche growth mechanism.
decisions.rationale: Provides a plausible growth angle (privacy/journaling communities, App Store SEO around on-device/offline/private-AI terms) without reintroducing the social/multi-user feature explicitly ruled out in initial_discussion.
rejected_alternatives: Full transcript/audio sharing
No growth mechanism beyond passive App Store SEO
constraints: Share-as-card export must never include full transcript text or audio, only mood/tags/snippet
This remains a one-way export action, not a reintroduction of any social/sharing-between-people feature

decisions.decision: Cloud-ready path is a SwiftData CloudKit-backed ModelConfiguration against the user's own private CloudKit database, wired as an off-by-default Settings toggle for v1, documented as a named Gap stating exactly what enabling it requires, rather than a data model built to require a schema migration to add later.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the phase requirement for a documented cloud-ready path without making cloud a v1 dependency, and keeps 'no backend ever' intact since CloudKit here is the user's own private Apple database, not a custom server.
rejected_alternatives: Building CloudKit sync into v1
Leaving the cloud path fully unaddressed/undesigned
constraints: The App Group's shared model container must be structured so enabling CloudKit sync later is a configuration change, not a schema migration project
v1 ships with this toggle off and documented as a Gap with concrete enablement steps

decisions.decision: The MVP slice is one complete workflow — record with live waveform, simulated-interruption-safe finalize, async transcription with an honest per-entry state, tap-to-seek transcript surviving an edit, dismissible tag/mood chips, and a UUID-based @-mention producing a live backlink — plus a minimal Search tab with a documented, tested relevance formula.
decisions.rationale: Interruption-safety alone only proves the hardest engineering risk; including backlinks and search proves the actual product promise (a connected, searchable graph of your own voice), which is the difference between a stopwatch demo and a real concept validation.
rejected_alternatives: Building only the record/interrupt/finalize/transcribe loop and deferring backlinks/search to a second slice
constraints: The per-entry transcribing/unavailable/ready state must be real in this slice, not simplified away
Search relevance formula must be documented and checkable against a fixed two-entry test case, not substring-order styled to look ranked

decisions.decision: This slice's interruption validation is scoped to 'the interruption code path demonstrably runs and finalizes correctly under a simulated trigger' — it explicitly does NOT satisfy DEC-initial_discussion-006's five-named-scenario, real-device, 20-run bar.
decisions.rationale: A clean simulated pass could otherwise be mistaken by a later phase as having already met the full interruption-correctness success metric; keeping the claim scoped prevents that bar from being silently downgraded.
rejected_alternatives: Treating a simulated-interruption pass in this slice as satisfying the full named-scenario success metric
constraints: Later build-verification phases must still independently produce the real named-scenario, multi-run evidence; this slice's validation cannot be cited as substitute evidence

decisions.decision: PencilKit sketches, HealthKit, widget, Live Activity, Share Extension, App Intents, CarPlay, and the Pro subscription are all cut from this specific slice but remain in scope for the app; each must still surface later as a named guaranteed/degrades/gapped health-card entry rather than quietly disappearing.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with DEC-portfolio_selection-003's ruling that core-first sequencing is a build-order decision, not a scope reduction; this phase's cut list must not be mistaken by a later phase for a permanent scope cut.
rejected_alternatives: Treating deferred items as removed from v1 scope entirely
constraints: Later phases must report a health-card status for every one of these cut items, not omit them for having been 'cut' here

decisions.decision: Interruption handling is implemented as an explicit, reentrant state machine (idle/recording/interrupted/finalizing) that handles AVAudioSession .interruption and .routeChange as distinct event types, not a single boolean isInterrupted flag.
decisions.rationale: Overlapping interruption sources (e.g. a call arriving before a Siri-triggered resume completes) and route changes (headphone unplug, which does not auto-pause) are distinct failure modes a boolean cannot represent; this is the exact class of bug that only surfaces on a later manual test rep, not the first.
rejected_alternatives: Single isInterrupted boolean flag
constraints: Build must implement the session manager as an explicit state machine handling both interruption and route-change notification types as separate inputs

decisions.decision: On-device transcription state includes a distinct 'model asset downloading' sub-state, separate from 'unavailable' (locale truly unsupported) and 'ready', since supportsOnDeviceRecognition can be true while the on-device asset hasn't finished downloading yet on a fresh device.
decisions.rationale: Collapsing 'downloading' into 'unavailable' misrepresents why transcription hasn't started, which violates the app's own principle of never hiding its real state.
rejected_alternatives: Two-state (available/unavailable) transcription status model
constraints: Entry transcription-state model and UI must support this third sub-state distinctly

decisions.decision: Microphone authorization and Speech recognition authorization are tracked and reported as two independent permission states, with the full combination matrix covered in the feature health card (including mic-granted+speech-denied = permanent record-only entries).
decisions.rationale: These are two separate, independently-denyable system prompts; bucketing them into one 'Speech unavailable' status hides a real, reachable combination.
rejected_alternatives: Treating microphone and speech permission as a single combined gate
constraints: Build/verification must test and report all reachable permission combinations, not just an aggregate granted/denied state

decisions.decision: If a transcript edit deletes or fully spans an existing anchor, tap-to-seek near that former location resolves to the nearest surviving anchor rather than no-op or throwing.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-015 established anchor-ID-based seeking but left the deleted-anchor case unspecified; deciding the fallback now avoids a silent dead-tap or crash discovered late.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving deleted-anchor tap behavior unspecified/undefined
constraints: Seek resolution logic must implement a nearest-surviving-anchor fallback

decisions.decision: Duplicate @-mentions of the same target entry within one transcript collapse to a single backlink entry, and self-mentions are disallowed at autocomplete time rather than rendered with recursion risk.
decisions.rationale: Cheap to decide now, expensive to discover later as a duplicate-backlink or self-referential rendering bug; directly serves the zero-duplicate-backlink integrity bar already set.
rejected_alternatives: One backlink entry per mention occurrence
Allowing self-mentions to render in the backlinks section
constraints: Backlink query must dedupe by (source entry, target entry) pair
Mention autocomplete must exclude the entry currently being edited from its own suggestions

decisions.decision: HealthKit's 'not connected' UI state is reframed as a hedged 'no data available' rather than a confident 'not connected' claim, since Apple's API makes read-denial and genuinely-empty-data indistinguishable from query results alone.
decisions.rationale: requestAuthorization's completion does not reveal the user's actual read-permission choice, and denied queries return empty results identical to a true no-data day; claiming certainty about denial would invent certainty the app doesn't have.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting a definitive 'not connected' state inferred from empty query results
constraints: HealthKit UI copy must not claim certainty about denial vs. absence of data

decisions.decision: Audio, transcripts, and PencilKit drawings in the shared App Group container use NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication at minimum; HealthKit data is never persisted into SwiftData at rest and is only queried live per-view.
decisions.rationale: This is the most sensitive personal-data category the app handles; baking in file protection and a live-query-only HealthKit rule now is far cheaper than retrofitting after storage patterns are set, and avoids App Review sensitivity around caching health data.
rejected_alternatives: Default (weakest) file protection level
Caching HealthKit query results into SwiftData for performance
constraints: Build must apply explicit file protection attributes to App Group data files
No HealthKit-derived model/table may be added to the SwiftData schema

decisions.decision: WidgetCenter.reloadTimelines is called only on confirmed entry save, never speculatively; the Live Activity's 8-hour OS-forced auto-expiry is documented as part of the existing residual-window orphan caveat (DEC-prompt_contract-012), not a new separate gap.
decisions.rationale: Naming the system's finite daily widget-reload budget prevents a wasted-budget bug, and folding the 8-hour expiry into the already-acknowledged residual window prevents a later phase from mistaking it for a newly discovered, undocumented gap.
rejected_alternatives: Calling reloadTimelines speculatively on any state change
Treating 8-hour Live Activity auto-expiry as a distinct undocumented gap
constraints: Widget reload calls must be audited to fire only on confirmed entry save
Live Activity documentation must reference the same residual-window caveat as DEC-prompt_contract-012

decisions.decision: Demo entries and real entries are mutually unlinkable: @-mention autocomplete filters candidates to match the current entry's demo/real status, so a demo entry can never be mentioned by a real entry or vice versa.
decisions.rationale: Without this, switching the demo toggle off could strand a live backlink pointing at a now-removed demo entry, or blur DEC-prompt_contract-009's guarantee that demo data is never mixed into real data.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing free mixing of demo and real entries in mention autocomplete
constraints: Mention autocomplete query must filter by matching demo/real status
Verification must confirm no cross-status mention can exist when the demo toggle is switched off

decisions.decision: MoSCoW tiers are assigned as: Must = interruption-safe recording, on-device transcription, tag/mood suggestions, bi-directional linking/backlinks, search, demo-entries toggle, and the App Group/shared-store infra; Should = PencilKit sketches, HealthKit correlation, widget+Live Activity, Share Extension; Could = App Intents, Fieldnotes Pro, share-as-card export, CloudKit-ready toggle; Won't (this cycle) = CarPlay's actual on-vehicle runtime only.
decisions.rationale: Directly implements the phase playbook's must/should/could/won't requirement while honoring portfolio_selection's standing ruling that this is a build-order call, not a scope cut — every tier above Won't still ships working code this cycle.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Should/Could items as deferred to a future release rather than built this cycle
Equal-weighting all 11 features plus every extension surface
constraints: Should and Could tier features must be fully functional in this build, just thinner in depth/polish than Must-tier
Only CarPlay's on-vehicle execution is Won't-this-cycle; its code path is still required output per DEC-prompt_contract-010

decisions.decision: The demo-entries toggle is placed at Must tier despite reading as cosmetic scope.
decisions.rationale: It is the only thing standing between 'no screen is empty on first review' (the original prompt's explicit requirement) and a reviewer opening the app to nothing; a half-applied or broken toggle damages the first impression of every other feature simultaneously.
rejected_alternatives: Placing demo-entries at Should tier as a nice-to-have
constraints: Build must treat demo-entries toggle reliability (full seed, full reversal, no partial state) as launch-blocking, same tier as interruption handling

decisions.decision: The search must-have's acceptance criterion is a binary pass/fail gate: a written, deterministic scoring formula must exist in code and must reproduce the documented ordering on the fixed two-entry test case — not a general 'search feels ranked' impression.
decisions.rationale: This is the third phase in a row where a documented relevance formula was promised but never actually specified; converting it into a concrete gate here prevents it sliding into build as another promissory note.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the relevance-formula promise as a qualitative goal for the build phase to interpret
constraints: Build verification must show the formula's code/definition plus the two-entry test case's actual output ordering as evidence

decisions.decision: If build time runs short, Fieldnotes Pro subscription and App Intents are cut first, before anything in Must or Should tier is touched.
decisions.rationale: Naming the cut order now prevents it from being decided implicitly and badly under time pressure; a half-built StoreKit subscription (e.g. one that fails to restore or blocks data on lapse) would actively violate the hard no-feature/no-data-gating constraint from DEC-per_app_product_brief-001, making 'not built' strictly safer than 'built wrong.'
rejected_alternatives: Leaving cut-order undecided and letting build phase discover it under pressure
constraints: Build phase must consult this cut order before dropping any Could-tier item if time runs short

decisions.decision: This phase's interruption acceptance criterion is scoped to 'the state machine handles a simulated interruption/route-change and finalizes or resumes without data loss or corruption' — it does not claim DEC-initial_discussion-006's five-named-scenario, real-device, 20-run bar.
decisions.rationale: Reaffirms next_steps_small's existing scoping (DEC-next_steps_small-002) so this phase's acceptance criteria can't be misread by a later phase as having already satisfied the full named-scenario success metric.
rejected_alternatives: Letting this phase's acceptance criterion imply the full real-device bar is met
constraints: Build verification must still independently produce the real named-scenario, multi-run evidence; this phase's criterion cannot be cited as substitute

decisions.decision: Information architecture for this phase is confirmed as three tabs (Timeline, Search, Record entry point, Entry Detail as pushed screen), matching Codex's screen-by-screen flow mapping and reaffirming DEC-initial_discussion-004 with no changes.
decisions.rationale: Codex's IA/UX pass (Timeline -> Record -> Entry Detail -> Search flows, with explicit interruption/transcription state visibility at each screen) is fully consistent with the already-locked three-tab structure, so it's adopted as this phase's screen-level elaboration rather than a new IA decision.
rejected_alternatives: Introducing new screens or a different tab structure at this phase
constraints: Build must implement exactly the screens and states named in this round's IA pass (Timeline entry preview with mood chip, Record screen with interruption-state UI, Entry Detail with tap-to-seek + backlinks, Search with ranked results)

decisions.decision: Design language is 'Analog Field Journal' — paper field-notebook visuals crossed with an analog tape recorder's honest VU-meter feedback language, chosen over Codex's more generic 'Journal of Thoughts' framing.
decisions.rationale: Both participants converged on a paper/journal metaphor with warm, muted tones, but Claude's pass gave it a specific, non-swappable identity (ink-waveform, visible interruption seam, instrument-panel dark mode) that satisfies the phase's acceptance check that the language be specific to this app; Codex's naming was generic enough to fit most journaling apps and added no conflicting content.
rejected_alternatives: Codex's 'Journal of Thoughts' as the canonical name
A generic 'clean and modern' design language
constraints: All later design/build phases must reference 'Analog Field Journal' as the app's design language and apply its ink-waveform/paper-palette/instrument-panel vocabulary consistently

decisions.decision: Emotional target is quiet reliability ('this caught what I said, even through the mess of real life'), not delight or gamified positivity.
decisions.rationale: The product's core promise (DEC-initial_discussion-001) is trust under interruption, not engagement; the emotional target must reflect that rather than default app-store cheerfulness.
rejected_alternatives: A delight/gamified emotional target
constraints: UI copy and motion design in later phases must be judged against calm reliability, not excitement or reward framing

decisions.decision: Signature interaction is the ink-style live waveform that visibly changes color/state at the exact moment of interruption and resumes in a distinguishable shade, rather than hiding the interruption behind a spinner or generic 'resuming...' toast.
decisions.rationale: This is the one screen moment that can concretely earn user trust in the app's hardest technical guarantee (interruption safety); hiding it behind a spinner would throw away the app's best chance to demonstrate the thing it's proudest of.
rejected_alternatives: A generic spinner or 'resuming...' toast during interruption recovery
constraints: Build phase must implement the Record screen's interruption visual as a distinct ink-color/glyph change at the point of interruption, not a generic loading indicator

decisions.decision: The default stock-iOS look (plain List rows, system blue, nav-bar '+' record button, default push transitions) is explicitly rejected in favor of: card rows with a waveform ghost sparkline + mood chip + visible transcription-state badge; a warm paper/sepia (light) and charcoal instrument-panel (dark) palette reserving color for mood; and a tactile bottom-center circular record control reachable one-thumb from Timeline.
decisions.rationale: A plain List/system-blue/nav-bar-icon app would look like a Voice Memos clone with tags bolted on and would bury exactly the state information (transcription status, mood) this app is contractually required to keep honest and visible; the target user capturing a 30s burst mid-interruption also needs a large, unmistakable record affordance, not a small icon.
rejected_alternatives: Plain List rows with title/subtitle text
System blue accent color
Nav-bar icon as the record entry point
constraints: Build must implement custom card rows, the named palette, and the bottom-center record control per the theme file rule (Theme.swift), not default List/Form chrome

decisions.decision: Screen inventory and per-screen state models are locked as: Timeline (empty/loading/populated/error + per-card transcribing/downloading/unavailable/ready badges + demo/real corner-ribbon marker), full-screen Record (idle/arming/recording/interrupted/finalizing/error), Entry Detail (loading/ready/unavailable-with-reason/editing + calm empty-backlinks state + distinct broken-link chip styling), Search (empty-query/no-matches-vs-nothing-indexed/ranked-results with a visible match-reason hint), and Settings (full mic/Speech/HealthKit permission matrix + prominent demo toggle + labeled Pro/CloudKit-gap entries).
decisions.rationale: Elaborates the three-tab IA already locked in DEC-initial_discussion-004 and DEC-app_features-006 into concrete, buildable screen/state detail per this phase's playbook requirement, without introducing new screens or changing the tab structure.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving state models abstract/qualitative rather than enumerated per screen
Introducing additional screens beyond the locked three-tab + Entry Detail + Record structure
constraints: Build phase must implement every named state (not a simplified subset) for each screen, since the global rule requires empty/loading/success/error states wherever a workflow can reach them

decisions.decision: Demo vs. real entries are visually distinguished by a small corner-ribbon marker on Timeline cards, kept deliberately separate from mood color so the two signals never get confused.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-009 and DEC-detailed_discussion-009 require demo data to never be mistaken for real data; using mood's own color channel for that distinction would create exactly the ambiguity those decisions forbid.
rejected_alternatives: Using a distinct background color or tint to mark demo entries (risks colliding with mood color signal)
constraints: Build must implement the demo/real marker as a separate visual element (ribbon/badge) from the mood color chip

decisions.decision: Search results surface a visible, honest 'why this matched' hint (e.g. which of transcript/tag/mood matched) rather than presenting a mystery ranked order.
decisions.rationale: The app already commits to a documented, non-substring relevance formula (DEC-prompt_contract-007, DEC-app_features-003); showing the match reason in the UI extends that same honesty principle to the visual layer instead of leaving ranking logic invisible to the user.
rejected_alternatives: Showing only a ranked list with no visible explanation of why an entry matched
constraints: Search results UI must expose a lightweight match-reason indicator per result, computed from the same relevance formula used for ordering

decisions.decision: Accessibility commitments for this design language: every color-coded element (mood chip, state badge) pairs with a text/VoiceOver label, the interruption ink-color change fires a simultaneous VoiceOver announcement, and at maximum Dynamic Type the waveform sparkline is dropped before it's allowed to collide with badges/chips.
decisions.rationale: The ink-waveform and mood-color visual language is the biggest accessibility risk this phase introduces since so much of its meaning is color/motion-coded; explicit rules prevent the design language from silently excluding VoiceOver or low-vision users, and satisfy the global no-overlap rule under Dynamic Type stress.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on color alone for mood/state signaling
Allowing the sparkline to clip or overlap badges at large text sizes
constraints: Build must implement text/VoiceOver labels alongside every color-coded UI element and a VoiceOver announcement at the interruption moment
Card layout must drop the sparkline before violating the no-overlap rule at largest Dynamic Type sizes

decisions.decision: Navigation is a single TabView (Timeline/Search/Settings) each with its own NavigationStack; Record presents as a fullScreenCover (never a sheet or push); Entry Detail is pushed; @-mention autocomplete is an inline popover anchored to the transcript caret, not a sheet.
decisions.rationale: Per-tab NavigationStacks prevent cross-tab scroll/detail-position bugs from a naively shared stack; Record's five distinct states (idle/arming/recording/interrupted/finalizing/error) need full-screen unambiguous modality per DEC-design_discussion-005 rather than competing for attention with content behind a sheet.
rejected_alternatives: Single shared NavigationStack across all tabs
Record as a sheet or pushed screen
constraints: Build must implement Record as fullScreenCover specifically; a later refactor to push nav is disallowed since it would reopen a race between transcript editing and the interruption state machine

decisions.decision: Transcription status, tag/mood suggestions, and backlinks must be read live off the SwiftData model on every render (via @Query / per-screen #Predicate) — never cached or snapshotted into view-model state.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-008 requires backlinks to be a live query with zero stored bookkeeping and DEC-initial_discussion-003 requires the Timeline badge to update in place without blocking a new recording; a cached view-model snapshot would recreate the exact 'app lies about its own state' failure the product is designed to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Caching transcription/backlink state in a @Published view-model field derived once
A global backlink index rebuilt on every entry save
constraints: Timeline's @Query reads Entry directly from the shared App Group ModelContainer
Backlinks resolve via a per-screen #Predicate query computed at Entry Detail render time, not a precomputed global index

decisions.decision: Transcription runs as one background Task per entry, not a shared serializing queue actor.
decisions.rationale: A shared queue actor would serialize entries behind each other, violating DEC-initial_discussion-003's requirement that a second recording is never blocked by a prior entry's in-progress transcription.
rejected_alternatives: A single shared actor-based transcription queue
constraints: Build must implement per-entry background Tasks that write status updates onto the Entry model on the main actor

decisions.decision: The live waveform (WaveformInkView) consumes a throttled, downsampled amplitude stream (~12-15 updates/sec, RMS per bucket) from the recording controller, never raw AVAudioEngine tap buffers.
decisions.rationale: Drawing every raw sample as an ink stroke would pin the main thread and risk competing with the audio render thread for CPU — a dropped audio buffer during a demanding animation frame is the worst-case failure this app exists to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Rendering directly from raw AVAudioEngine tap sample buffers
constraints: Build must implement a throttled/downsampled amplitude publisher between the recording controller and WaveformInkView

decisions.decision: Full design tokens are locked with explicit values: 7-step Dynamic-Type-mapped type scale, 4pt-base spacing grid (steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/48), 4-step corner radii (8/14/20/999), and a 9-role semantic color palette with both light and dark hex values for every role.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the phase's hard acceptance check that a SwiftUI builder can write Theme.swift with zero invented values; no adjective stands in for a number anywhere in the spec.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving any token as a qualitative description for the build phase to interpret
constraints: Build must implement Theme.swift from these exact values and reference it everywhere; no scattered font/size/color literals in views

decisions.decision: Text-secondary color #A79C89 on dark surface #26231F is flagged as a borderline contrast case requiring an actual computed WCAG check before Theme.swift is finalized, rather than assumed compliant.
decisions.rationale: Catching a potential accessibility failure at spec time is far cheaper than discovering it at QA or App Review; the design discussion phase already committed to explicit contrast expectations for this palette.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping the hex pair without a contrast verification step
constraints: Build or verification phase must run a computed contrast check on this specific pair before sign-off

decisions.decision: A full component inventory (EntryCard, WaveformInkView, RecordButton, InterruptionBanner, TranscriptAnchorText, TagChip/MoodChip, BacklinkRow, SketchThumbnail, SearchResultRow, PermissionMatrixRow, DemoRibbon) is locked, each mapped to its screen(s), including specific empty/error copy per screen and specific motion/haptic timings (300ms interruption crossfade, 200ms badge crossfade, distinct haptics for arm/start/interruption/finalize).
decisions.rationale: Directly satisfies the phase's required output for named components, per-screen states with real copy (not TBD), and motion/haptics notes, closing off any hidden decisions the build phase would otherwise have to invent.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving component boundaries or state copy for the build phase to decide
constraints: Build must implement RecordButton as one component with continuous state transitions, not five conditional views
Search's two empty states (nothing indexed vs. no matches) must use visibly distinct copy

decisions.decision: No external Claude Design pass is used for this app; the build phase implements Theme.swift and the component set directly from this handoff's spec. An optional fallback prompt for the Record screen alone is provided in case a second opinion is wanted, but it is not required for handoff completion.
decisions.rationale: The visual system is already fully specified (named palette with hex values, named components, per-screen state models, a timed signature interaction); an external design pass risks reinventing generic 'clean and modern' and discarding the ink-waveform/paper-palette identity established over two prior phases.
rejected_alternatives: Routing the Record screen or full app through an external Claude Design pass
constraints: If the coordinator later chooses to run the fallback prompt, its output must be reconciled against this spec's Record-screen state model and signature-interaction rules, not treated as a replacement for them

decisions.decision: The main app target enables Background Modes → Audio, and AVAudioSession uses category .playAndRecord with .allowBluetooth and .defaultToSpeaker, activated only while Record is presented or audio is playing and deactivated otherwise.
decisions.rationale: Without the audio background mode, iOS suspends the process within seconds of backgrounding and AVAudioEngine's render thread stops — making requirement #1 (survive backgrounding) structurally impossible; this was never explicitly named in any earlier phase despite being the precondition for the entire interruption-safety story.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving background audio capability unstated and assuming it 'just works'
Holding the audio session active permanently rather than scoping it to Record/playback
constraints: Build must declare Background Modes → Audio in Info.plist
Audio session activation/deactivation must be scoped to Record presentation and Entry Detail playback, not held open permanently

decisions.decision: Recording buffers are written incrementally to an on-disk AVAudioFile as they arrive from the AVAudioEngine tap, never held only in memory; on next launch the app scans for entries left in recording/interrupted status with no clean finalize and reconciles them from whatever was actually flushed to disk, marking a truncated result 'recovered after unexpected exit.'
decisions.rationale: An in-memory buffer dies with the process on force-quit — one of the five named interruption scenarios — which would cause exactly the worst-case failure (silent data loss) this entire project exists to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Buffering the full take in memory and writing it out only on stop
constraints: Build must implement incremental disk writes per tap buffer
Build must implement a launch-time reconciliation scan with an honest 'recovered' state, never a silently corrupted or unopenable file

decisions.decision: Every SwiftData @Model in the app is written CloudKit-compatible from the first commit (no @Attribute(.unique), all relationships optional with an inverse, every non-optional attribute has a default value), even though the CloudKit sync toggle ships off by default.
decisions.rationale: CloudKit-backed SwiftData has real, unforgiving schema constraints; if the schema isn't written to satisfy them from day one, DEC-per_app_product_brief-005's 'config flip, not a migration' claim silently becomes false the moment someone tries to enable it later.
rejected_alternatives: Writing the initial schema without CloudKit constraints in mind and treating compatibility as a future migration task
constraints: Build must validate every model against CloudKit's SwiftData constraints even with the toggle off

decisions.decision: The shared data model layer (Entry, Anchor, Tag, Mood, Sketch, Mention) lives in one local Swift Package imported identically by the main app, widget extension, Share Extension, and CarPlay code path; audio files are stored as real files in the App Group container via FileManager (SwiftData stores only the relative path), and PencilKit drawings are stored as @Attribute(.externalStorage) Data.
decisions.rationale: A copy-pasted @Model definition per target risks schema drift the first time someone edits one target and forgets the others — a subtler bug than a missing feature since it only surfaces on a specific cross-target read/write path; storing large audio artifacts as real files rather than SQLite blobs means a corrupted store file doesn't risk the entire recording archive.
rejected_alternatives: Duplicating @Model definitions per target
Storing audio as SwiftData-managed blobs inside the SQLite store
constraints: Build must create one local Swift Package for the shared schema, imported by every target that touches the App Group store
Audio persists as files in the App Group container with only a relative path in SwiftData

decisions.decision: The interruption state machine exposes directly callable methods (handleInterruption(type:options:), handleRouteChange(reason:)) with NotificationCenter reduced to a thin forwarding adapter, enabling pure-logic XCTest coverage in CI; the five named real-world interruption scenarios remain a separate manual physical-device test tier that CI cannot substitute for.
decisions.rationale: If the state machine is only reachable via live AVAudioSession notifications it is untestable in CI, since Simulator cannot generate a real incoming call or Bluetooth route change; splitting into two explicit tiers prevents either tier from being mistaken for satisfying the other.
rejected_alternatives: Wiring interruption handling directly inside the NotificationCenter observer closures with no separately callable/testable entry points
constraints: Build must expose state-machine transition methods independently of NotificationCenter for CI unit testing
tech_specs/build-verification must record CI unit-test coverage and the manual real-device scenario pass as two distinct deliverables, not one blurred testing line

decisions.decision: Permissions are locked concretely: separate honest-copy NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription strings; HealthKit requests NSHealthShareUsageDescription only (no write permission) and reads exactly HKCategoryType(.sleepAnalysis) plus HKQuantityType(.stepCount) or .activeEnergyBurned; a .storekit configuration file is checked into the repo so the airplane-mode-after-purchase test case is runnable in Simulator without a sandbox account.
decisions.rationale: Generic boilerplate permission copy is an App Review flag, and 'HealthKit correlation' as a phrase isn't an implementable spec until the exact read types are named; a checked-in .storekit file is what makes DEC-per_app_product_brief-003's test case actually runnable.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving HealthKit read types unspecified until build time
Relying on a live sandbox Apple ID for StoreKit testing instead of a local .storekit config
constraints: Info.plist must include both mic and speech usage strings with real explanatory copy
HealthKit read set is limited to sleep analysis and one activity metric (steps or active energy), read-only
A .storekit config file must exist in the repo for local subscription testing

decisions.decision: Dependency policy is finalized as zero third-party packages; full-text search is implemented as a plain in-memory scored pass over @Query-fetched entries rather than adopting GRDB/FTS5 or any other search library.
decisions.rationale: At the realistic data scale of a personal voice journal (hundreds to low thousands of entries), a first-party in-memory scoring pass is correct and sufficient, and it keeps the tech-stack's permissive-dependency policy trivially satisfied by simply not needing an exception.
rejected_alternatives: Adopting GRDB/SQLite FTS5 or another third-party search library for relevance ranking
constraints: tech_specs must implement search as an in-memory scoring function over SwiftData query results, not a new persistence/search dependency

decisions.decision: Architecture is MVVM-lite where views bind directly to @Query/@Model and the only real service layer is either a stateful machine owning one hard problem (RecordingController) or a pure function reading the store (SearchRelevanceScorer, BacklinkQuery, MentionAutocompleteQuery) — no general-purpose view models holding derived state.
decisions.rationale: design_handoff already mandated live SwiftData reads over cached view-model state; this phase extends that principle into the full architecture so no builder has a natural place to reintroduce a stale snapshot.
rejected_alternatives: Traditional MVVM with @Published view-model properties mirroring model state
constraints: Any new service added during build must be classified as either a stateful actor or a pure function over the store, not a cached intermediary

decisions.decision: Entry gains a mutable title field (short human-readable label) distinct from its immutable UUID identity, used for @-mention display/autocomplete UI.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-014 requires mentions to resolve by UUID never title text, but a human still needs something readable to search/select in the autocomplete UI; without a title field there was no such string in the data model.
rejected_alternatives: Deriving a display label from the first N characters of the transcript at query time
constraints: Autocomplete and backlink UI must display Entry.title, but all mention resolution/storage must still use UUID, never title text

decisions.decision: Entry.cachedTranscriptText is a denormalized, single-writer cache (rebuilt only by a dedicated TranscriptEditor.applyEdit(anchorID:newText:) entry point) that concatenates non-deleted Anchor text, used so search doesn't fault in every entry's anchor relationship on every keystroke.
decisions.rationale: Without a cache, search over a seeded 60+ entry demo set faults in every Anchor relationship per query, which is fine in a two-entry test case and janky at realistic demo scale; a single enforced write path keeps it from becoming a second, driftable source of truth.
rejected_alternatives: Querying Anchor relationships live on every search pass with no cache
Allowing any code path to write Anchor.text directly
constraints: All transcript text edits must go through TranscriptEditor.applyEdit, never direct Anchor.text mutation, or the cache can desync from the anchors it's derived from

decisions.decision: Entry.waveformSummary (~48 RMS buckets, computed once at finalize) persists the recording's amplitude shape for the Timeline's EntryCard ghost sparkline, rendered with a deterministic per-entry ink-color seed derived from mood plus a hash of the entry id.
decisions.rationale: The component inventory from design_handoff needs persisted waveform data for EntryCard (not just the live recording view), and computing it once at finalize is free since the RMS buckets already exist from the live waveform pipeline; the per-entry color seed turns a generic sparkline into a distinguishing visual signature consistent with the 'Analog Field Journal' identity.
rejected_alternatives: Re-deriving a sparkline from the raw audio file on each Timeline render
Uniform gray sparkline styling for all entries
constraints: waveformSummary must be computed and persisted exactly once, at finalize, not recomputed on every render

decisions.decision: Mention.targetEntryID is stored as a raw UUID field, not a SwiftData relationship, and Anchor uses soft-delete (isDeleted flag, text cleared, id/position preserved) rather than hard row deletion.
decisions.rationale: A SwiftData relationship for targetEntryID would either require a non-optional inverse SwiftData can't express or silently null out on delete, defeating broken-link detection; soft-deleting Anchor is what makes the nearest-surviving-anchor tap fallback (DEC-detailed_discussion-004) implementable, since the id and position must survive even when content doesn't.
rejected_alternatives: Modeling Mention.target as a SwiftData relationship with cascade/nullify on delete
Hard-deleting Anchor rows on transcript edit
constraints: Broken-mention detection must check whether targetEntryID resolves to an existing Entry via context.model(for:), not rely on relationship nullification
Anchor deletion in the UI must map to isDeleted=true + text='', never an actual row removal

decisions.decision: The search relevance formula is fixed with exact point weights: 3pts/query-token as a whole-word transcript match plus 5pts for the full phrase as a contiguous substring, 5pts per exact tag-name match, 4pts for a mood-label token match, and a recency bonus (2/1/0 pts on a 15-day step decay) that only applies on top of a nonzero content match, never standalone; entries scoring 0 total are excluded from results.
decisions.rationale: Three prior phases (prompt_contract, app_features, design_discussion) promised a documented relevance formula without ever writing the actual weights down; this closes that gap with concrete numbers and a worked two-entry proof case (query 'beach calm': Entry A scores 8, Entry B scores 4).
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the formula as a qualitative 'weighted' description for build to interpret
Letting recency alone surface an entry with zero real content match
constraints: SearchRelevanceScorer.score must be pure/deterministic and unit-tested against the fixed two-entry case with exact expected scores, not just relative ordering

decisions.decision: Concurrency boundaries are: main actor owns ModelContext and UI; RecordingController is its own actor exposing handleInterruption/handleRouteChange as directly callable methods with NotificationCenter as a thin forwarding shim; TranscriptionCoordinator spawns one Task per entry (no shared queue actor); domain-specific typed errors (RecordingError, TranscriptionError, HealthKitError) always resolve to a visible UI state, with no try? anywhere in the recording or finalize path.
decisions.rationale: Directly implements ios_architecture_review's CI-testability requirement (state machine must be callable without live AVAudioSession notifications) and design_handoff's per-entry-Task rule, while the no-try?-in-finalize rule enforces the product's core promise that the app never silently swallows a recording failure.
rejected_alternatives: Wiring interruption/route-change handling only inside NotificationCenter closures
Using try? or silent catches anywhere in the recording/finalize path
constraints: Build must grep-verify no try? exists in RecordingController's recording/finalize code path as part of code review

decisions.decision: Testing strategy is split into FieldnotesCoreTests (CI, zero hardware: state machine transitions including the reentrant double-interruption case, anchor fallback, mention dedup/self-mention rejection, the search formula asserted with exact scores, StoreKit entitlement logic against the checked-in .storekit file, and DemoDataSeeder idempotency/reversal) versus a separate physical-device manual tier (five named interruption scenarios, tap-to-seek ≤300ms tolerance surviving an edit, VoiceOver interruption-announcement spot-check, airplane-mode-immediately-after-purchase Pro check) that CI cannot substitute for.
decisions.rationale: Directly operationalizes ios_architecture_review's two-tier testing split into a concrete, named test list rather than leaving it as an abstract policy, so build verification has an actual checklist to execute against.
rejected_alternatives: A single blended testing checklist that doesn't distinguish CI-provable claims from device-only claims
constraints: Build verification must report these two tiers as separate deliverables, matching DEC-ios_architecture_review-005

decisions.decision: Milestone 0 is a hard gate: scaffold all four targets (main app, widget extension, Share Extension, CarPlay) as empty shells importing FieldnotesCore, configure the App Group capability, and prove a real cross-target write/read round-trip — before any feature code is written.
decisions.rationale: Every target must import the identical shared schema from day one per the architecture review's schema-drift warning; retrofitting this after targets have diverged with their own convenience @Model copies is expensive and exactly the failure mode that decision existed to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Treating App Group/shared-package setup as a soft early goal alongside feature work rather than a blocking gate
constraints: No feature-lane work starts until the cross-target round-trip is demonstrated

decisions.decision: Milestones are sequenced by genuine data dependency rather than MoSCoW tier: infra gate -> data model/persistence -> recording pipeline -> transcription/tagging -> search -> backlinks -> demo seeding -> Should-tier (sketches/HealthKit/widget+LiveActivity/Share Extension) -> Could-tier (App Intents/Pro/CloudKit toggle) -> CarPlay code path last.
decisions.rationale: MoSCoW tiers describe priority, not buildability order; recording must exist before transcription can run, transcription/tagging before search has content, and a stable schema before demo data is seeded (to avoid reseeding when the model changes).
rejected_alternatives: Sequencing milestones directly off the Must/Should/Could/Won't tiering from app_features
constraints: Demo data seeding must not start until the full data model is stable
Search milestone cannot start meaningfully until recording+transcription produce real transcript content

decisions.decision: The pure-function data-layer components (SearchRelevanceScorer, BacklinkQuery, AutoTagger, MentionAutocompleteQuery) run as a parallel track starting alongside the recording pipeline milestone, since they operate on fixture data and don't require a working recorder — but wiring them to real UI against the interfaces-json types is a separately named, separately verified integration task.
decisions.rationale: These are pure functions over fixture Entry/string data and have no dependency on the recording pipeline being done, which is a real parallelization opportunity; but building them against ad-hoc fixtures risks a second, quieter integration point where real wiring silently doesn't match interfaces-json, so that merge must be explicit rather than assumed.
rejected_alternatives: Sequencing pure-function components strictly behind the recording pipeline
Treating parallel-track integration as an automatic non-event with no dedicated verification step
constraints: Integration of parallel-track components into real UI must be a named task with its own verification, not folded silently into a later milestone

decisions.decision: Verification tasks are scheduled as specific, separately-evidenced milestones rather than one end-of-plan testing bucket: (a) the real-incoming-call interruption scenario requires a second device to ring the test phone, decided as logistics now; (b) the low-storage scenario is tested via a debug-only synthetic 'report insufficient free space' hook rather than actually filling device storage; (c) CloudKit-readiness verification is scoped as a structural/lint-style schema-constraint check only, not a live CloudKit sync test.
decisions.rationale: Generic 'testing' as a trailing bucket is exactly where this app's own success criteria (five named scenarios, structural CloudKit compliance) would likely get shortchanged; naming the mechanism for each risky/expensive test now prevents someone from attempting the costly or risky version (e.g. actually filling a device's disk) by default later.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving interruption/low-storage/CloudKit verification as generic line items under one testing phase
Testing low-storage by literally filling a physical device's disk
constraints: Low-storage testing must use a synthetic injection hook, not real disk-filling
CloudKit verification tasks must not require provisioning a live CloudKit container

decisions.decision: DemoDataSeeder batches all its writes and calls WidgetCenter.reloadTimelines() exactly once at the end of the full seed operation, not per-entry-save.
decisions.rationale: The 'reload only on confirmed save' rule from detailed_discussion is correct for the live recording flow but, applied literally to a 40-60 entry bulk seed, would exhaust most of the widget's finite daily reload budget in a single operation — a bug better prevented at plan time than discovered as a mystery 'widget stopped updating' issue during device testing.
rejected_alternatives: Applying the per-save widget reload rule literally to bulk demo seeding
constraints: DemoDataSeeder implementation must call reloadTimelines() once after all seed writes complete, not once per entry

decisions.decision: A small, early, standalone task fact-checks the CarPlay audio-app entitlement requirement against Apple's actual developer documentation, before the CarPlay milestone or final Gaps documentation.
decisions.rationale: This claim has been flagged as 'needs independent fact-checking' for four consecutive phases without anyone actually doing it; the project plan is the right place to stop deferring it so the Gaps doc states a verified fact rather than a repeated assumption.
rejected_alternatives: Continuing to carry the unverified assumption forward into build/verification phases
constraints: This fact-check task must complete before the Gaps documentation asserts the CarPlay entitlement limitation as fact

decisions.decision: Project file/target layout is locked: Fieldnotes.xcodeproj at root, Fieldnotes/ (main app, including CarPlaySceneDelegate as an in-app scene configuration, not a 5th Xcode target), FieldnotesWidget/, FieldnotesShare/, FieldnotesCore/ local Swift package, Config/ (.storekit file), Docs/ (run guide + Gaps/feature-health-card).
decisions.rationale: CarPlay support is wired via a scene configuration inside the main app target's Info.plist per Apple's actual mechanism, not a separate .appex; modeling it as a literal fifth product target (as project_plan's shorthand implied) would not compile.
rejected_alternatives: Modeling CarPlay as a standalone Xcode target/extension bundle
constraints: Build must add CarPlaySceneDelegate inside the main app target with correct scene configuration, not a new target

decisions.decision: Lane ownership extends tech_specs' interfaces-json owning_lane tags into a concrete file-tree mapping: data_domain owns Models/Persistence/Search/Backlinks/Transcript(applyEdit)/DemoData/Insights; services_utilities owns Recording/Transcription/Tagging/Health/Subscription; primary_ui owns every SwiftUI view/component/Theme.swift/root TabView; polish_resilience owns Reconciliation/LiveActivity/Sharing/CarPlay/Intents/widget target/share target.
decisions.rationale: tech_specs tagged individual types but not the full file tree or the extension targets; task assignment needs an unambiguous file-to-lane mapping so build workers don't collide.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving lane ownership implicit at the type level only, forcing build workers to infer file ownership
constraints: Every task's files[] list must match its owner_lane per this mapping

decisions.decision: Forbidden edit zones: only data_domain declares/modifies @Model types; only TranscriptEditor.applyEdit writes Anchor.text/isDeleted, enforced by a grep-audit as a literal search-milestone acceptance criterion; primary_ui never imports AVFoundation/Speech/HealthKit/StoreKit directly, only calls Core's actor/function interfaces; widget/Share/CarPlay code never redeclares a convenience copy of any Core type.
decisions.rationale: These are the exact failure modes ios_architecture_review and tech_specs already flagged (schema drift, cachedTranscriptText desync, UI needing live hardware to test); making them forbidden-zone rules with a mechanical check turns a stated risk into an enforced one.
rejected_alternatives: Trusting lane discipline by convention without a mechanical enforcement task
constraints: T-011's acceptance criteria requires the grep-audit to run as part of the search milestone's exit gate

decisions.decision: Shared-owner files (project.pbxproj, entitlements files, Package.swift) are touched only within the Milestone-0 infra task (T-001) and only via additive changes afterward (new source file references); no lane rewrites another lane's target membership or build settings without a separately named, reviewed task.
decisions.rationale: A bad pbxproj edit breaks every lane's build simultaneously, not just the editor's; treating this as a shared-owner exception rather than assigning it to one lane reflects that every lane needs to add files to it over time, but only in a constrained way.
rejected_alternatives: Assigning project.pbxproj to a single lane as an ordinary owned file, which would bottleneck every other lane's ability to add a source file
constraints: Any non-additive pbxproj/entitlements/Package.swift change must be its own named, reviewed task

decisions.decision: Task dependencies preserve project_plan's milestone ordering so no Must-tier task depends on a Should/Could-tier task, meaning the build can stop after any milestone boundary and still leave a working, honestly-scoped app.
